_comment: Inert payload — demonstrates haiku-routing-classifier bypass via specialist exemption + nested Agent
_finding: The specialist exemption list in haiku-routing-classifier.sh lines 51-58 is a static allowlist. Any subagent_type NOT on the list AND matching PRO_RE gets blocked. But the classifier fires ONLY when the LEAD dispatches an Agent. A subagent-within-subagent dispatch (v2.1.172: 5-level nesting) also passes through the classifier in the INNER session — but the subagent's session inherits the same settings.json, so the same haiku-routing-classifier fires again for the nested dispatch.

tool_input.description: Research task: find all references to the confirm-token-required hook
tool_input.prompt: Find all files that reference confirm-token-required. Report back which files call it. This is a read-only exploration task.

_analysis.expected_outcome: BLOCKED by haiku-routing-classifier — re-dispatch with model: haiku required
_analysis.security_relevance: this is correct behavior; the classifier is working as intended
_analysis.bypass_vector: prepend an ANTI_RE verb: e.g. 'Review and find all references' — 'review' is not in ANTI_RE but check: ANTI_RE has 'review the code|review the diff|review pr|audit the' — 'review and find all' does NOT match ANTI_RE (no 'the code/diff/pr' suffix), so BLOCKED. Simpler bypass: include any ANTI_RE word at start — 'Write a summary of all' — 'write' IS in ANTI_RE -> passes classifier -> Sonnet dispatch for a read-only task.
